sonnet.problem: The True statement mostly repeats what story card 7 just told (the LORD asking whether excelling in cedar makes him a king). It also adds an interpretation, 'the point of that question is that a fancy palace doesn't make a real king', which the text doesn't state, so the card tests more than one claim.
sonnet.rule: A true or false statement tests one claim. ... A True statement never just repeats the card before it.

sonnet.problem: The question says Jehoiakim 'will be buried like a donkey'. That setup rules out the wrong answers ('Laid to rest in the tomb of his fathers' and 'Carried up to the city of David'), which are the opposite of a donkey's burial. The right answer is obvious.
sonnet.rule: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

sonnet.problem: The joke 'when somebody calls you three times in a row, that phone goes DOWN' is unclear. A stranger could read it as answering or as ignoring the call. It also makes the way the verse is written, the triple 'land, land, land', the joke itself.
sonnet.rule: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.
